code.heading: 10. Tree Map
code.code:
# Import required libraries
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import squarify # install if you do not have it

# Sample data
data = {
    'File Type': ['Documents', 'Videos', 'Images', 'Audio', 'Other'],
    'Storage Used (GB)': [50, 150, 80, 60, 10]
}

# Create a pandas dataframe from the dictionary
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Plotting the treemap
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
colors = ['red', 'green', 'blue', 'yellow', 'grey']
squarify.plot(sizes=df['Storage Used (GB)'], label=df['File Type'], color=colors, alpha=0.6)

# Add title
plt.title('Storage Used by File Type')
plt.axis('off')  # Turn off the axis

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('./outputs/plots/treemap.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

# Display the plot
plt.show()

code.heading: 11. Geographical Maps
code.code:
# Import required libraries
import plotly.graph_objects as go

# Data for cities and their coordinates
cities = {
    'New York': [40.7128, -74.0060],
    'London': [51.5074, -0.1278],
    'Sydney': [-33.8688, 151.2093],
    'Tokyo': [35.6895, 139.6917],
    'Rio de Janeiro': [-22.9068, -43.1729]
}

# Extracting latitudes, longitudes, and city names for plotting
lats = [coords[0] for coords in cities.values()]
longs = [coords[1] for coords in cities.values()]
names = list(cities.keys())

# Creating the Scattergeo plot
fig = go.Figure(data=go.Scattergeo(
    lon = longs,
    lat = lats,
    text = names,
    mode = 'markers',
    marker = dict(
        size = 10,
        opacity = 0.8,
        reversescale = True,
        autocolorscale = False,
        symbol = 'circle',
        line = dict(
            width=1,
            color='rgba(102, 102, 102)'
        ),
    )
))

# Setting the layout for the map
fig.update_layout(
    title = 'Cities on World Map using Plotly',
    geo = dict(
        scope='world',
        showland = True,
    )
)

# ... (truncated)

code.heading: 6. Heatmap
code.code:
# import required libraries
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Sample correlation matrix
data = {
    'Product A': [1, 0.6, 0.8, 0.3],
    'Product B': [0.6, 1, 0.5, 0.7],
    'Product C': [0.8, 0.5, 1, 0.4],
    'Product D': [0.3, 0.7, 0.4, 1]
}

# Create a pandas dataframe from the dictionary
df = pd.DataFrame(data)

# Plotting the heatmap
plt.figure(figsize=(8, 6))
sns.heatmap(df, annot=True, cmap='viridis', vmin=0, vmax=1)

# Set the title of the plot
plt.title('Product Correlation Heatmap')

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('./outputs/plots/heatmap.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

# Display the plot
plt.show()

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using When to use map vs apply vs applymap on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
